idea.why: Real crew decomposition rather than one mega-prompt: a triage specialist per source, then an editor that owns only presentation. Each concern lives in exactly one place, and both source agents carry explicit empty-input fallbacks, so the design anticipates a quiet day. Loses points only because the dashboard exists solely as an outbound email.

structure.why: Aggregate is the correct purpose-built way to collapse items instead of the usual Code-node reinvention, and the wait-for-all Merge is a legitimate barrier, not ceremony. Two dings: all three agent nodes carry no tools or memory, which a chain covers, and a fence-stripping regex is doing an output parser's job inline.

connections.why: Textbook. The trigger fans out to the two independent fetches instead of serialising them, each source runs its own linear chain, and the streams rejoin precisely where they genuinely become one document. One model node is fanned out to all three agents rather than duplicated.

answer.why: End to end this does what was asked and a reader would recognise their request. The weak seam is that the two specialists hand the editor free-form text, so an odd inbox degrades silently, and the whole thing rests on the model emitting clean HTML with only a regex as a safety net.

appraisal: Finds the right shape: two independent source agents in parallel off one trigger, a merge barrier where they genuinely rejoin, and a single editor that owns rendering, with one model fanned out to all three. It is thoughtful about real data where others are not, with alwaysOutputData and explicit empty-day fallbacks so a quiet Sunday still produces a valid briefing. The soft spots are the free-text handoff between agents, which loses structure the editor then has to re-parse, and the fenced-code regex standing in for a proper parser. The first change would be making the source agents emit structured JSON so the editor consumes fields rather than prose; the second, serving the HTML from a webhook so the dashboard is somewhere you can open, not only something landing in the inbox it just triaged.
